brief: GS's equities desk (Garber) reports quiet US futures after Monday's AI-led rally (AI Semis +5%, NeoClouds +6%, Mag7 +3.2%), with SMH and META fading premarket. Iran reportedly offered to reopen Hormuz within 7 days if the US eases military pressure, and Saudi Arabia restarted its East-West pipeline and prepared to resume Yanbu exports. Both moves pushed WTI down 2.6% to $93.30 and UST yields lower. Trader Privo stays constructive on AI (frontier-AI thesis intact, expects rivals to ship Muse-like apps) but favors bottlenecks, rails, and proprietary data over human-friction plays, and flags little room for defensives if growth holds. Separately, GS's economics team reversed its no-hike call: Middle East-driven energy prices, a 3.3% Q3 GDP track, and August payrolls (+162k) pushed core PCE to 0.27% month-over-month, so the FOMC hiked 25bp and 16 of 18 participants dot one more hike by the October 27-28 meeting, expected despite midterm proximity. GS's commodities team still sees crude falling to $85 by year-end and $75 by 2027, with energy passthrough explaining under half of the 3.1% core PCE overshoot. Desk flows: asset managers net bought $779mm, hedge funds net sold $974mm.
